top.line: A web of trust for careers: keys in people's own repositories, two-way links, countersigned jobs and degrees.

in-short.line: Keys and repositories, two-way links, countersignatures, link lists, agents walk the graph, a business.

problem.line: No good way to check who worked or studied where, and connections that mean little.

have.line: pki.sgit.ai, its four rules from the 2019 keyserver failure, agent keys and QR codes already exist.

identity.line: Several identities per person, keys in a repository they control, the one behind their site.

links.line: Sign by QR in person; a link counts only when both sides publish it; one-way links mean nothing.

work.line: The person claims a job or a degree; the company or university countersigns; nothing published unasked.

links-not-revocation.line: Publish what is valid: a link holds while both sides still publish it; git keeps the history.

graph.line: Checks are plain reads, so following the graph scales; each person's AI does the work.

no-recommendations.line: Connections and confirmations only; credibility from the shape of the graph.

organisations.line: Every organisation needs one internally: staff, roles and agents, signed and versioned.

europe.line: A professional network for Europe where nobody owns the graph, alongside the EU wallet and credentials.

business.line: Free for people; organisations pay to confirm; verification as a service; an internal edition.

names.line: Countersign, Mutual, Vouch, Trellis, Nexo; Countersign for the mechanism, Mutual for the network.

limits.line: A proposal on existing pieces; the step count an estimate; no countersigned job yet.

sources.line: My thinking, pki.sgit.ai's rules and history, and the standards, on 21 November 2026.
